name: Kingdom of Naples
alt: Kingdom of Sicily on this side of the Faro

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Sicily
predecessors.text: the mainland that Charles of Anjou kept after the 1282 rebellion lost him the island of Sicily

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: Treaty of Granada: Louis would receive the northern regions, including Abruzzo and Terra di Lavoro; Naples itself surrendered to the French in August 1501

successors.name: Crown of Aragon
successors.text: Treaty of Granada: Ferdinand would receive Calabria and the Apulian territories of Terra di Bari and Terra di Otranto

ledger.x: 1282: after the Sicilian Vespers Charles of Anjou loses the island of Sicily but keeps the mainland, the Kingdom of Naples.
1302: the Peace of Caltabellotta fixes the name Kingdom of Sicily Citra Farum.
1442: Alfonso V of Aragon conquers the Kingdom of Naples and holds it with Sicily as a dependency of Aragon.
1458: Alfonso V dies and Naples passes to his illegitimate son Ferdinand I as a separate kingdom.
1501: the French and Spanish armies over-run the kingdom; Ferdinand's share is Calabria, Terra di Bari and Terra di Otranto.
1501: Capua falls on 24 July and Frederick surrenders Naples to the French in August.
1501: the Aragonese kingdom of Naples ends when Frederick gives up the capital to Louis XII; exiled to France, he dies in 1504.

wars.name: War of the Sicilian Vespers
wars.outcome: Charles of Anjou lost the island and kept the mainland, the Kingdom of Naples; the Peace of Caltabellotta (1302) set the mainland kingdom's name as Kingdom of Sicily Citra Farum.

wars.name: Italian War of 1494-1495
wars.outcome: Charles VIII captured Naples without a fight on 22 February 1495 after Alfonso II abdicated for Ferdinand II, left for Lombardy on 20 May and the Aragonese defeated the French garrison on 6-7 July 1495; the castle held out to 8 December 1495.

wars.name: French and Spanish partition and conquest of Naples
wars.outcome: Treaty of Granada (11 November 1500) partitioned the kingdom; Capua fell 24 July 1501 and Frederick surrendered Naples in August; the allies fell out over Basilicata, Principato and Capitanata, war resumed in late 1502 and by the end of 1503 the French were…
